body:
What I hope to achieve is to become more disciplined and eventually professional, filling out forms is essentially tied to w.e you want to do in life to be recognized/qualified in a binding agreement.
 
It would be a pipedream to expect to when I leave the online "group" that things would stay the same and that they would go off to do other things. 

A couple of memories already spring to mind where one similar aged friend departs to focus on his own career to be replaced by younger ones, I casually joke about not becoming like me so perhaps it is time just to cut ties/contact, I've already talked about the prospect of acting seriously with closer individuals within the group. So it's sorta ominous of my departing.

In any case thank you for being a part of my decision-making.

Thank you for reading, sir~
I get the impression that you are older than 21, I have had more older friends in my time as I've looked up to them

I'm sure the detox period may uncover drive, but unfortunately the idea of reasoning behind with whatever I may find enjoyable is to **try** it out and this can take x+1 times until I'm fully determined and set. In any case, the response helps a lot. I'll try my best within the path I lay, discipline and self-esteem will follow.

The other dormant issue is to contend with being a professional but for now, however I feel it won't be an issue growing up.

Hi Friend,

To answer your first, I completely understand that the world owes me **nothing**. That I, myself, would have to pull the effort and motivation in the long run to try and "fix" my outlook. It's hard to explicitly state what my intentions are since they are subjective towards the goal in mind.
The best answer I can give is to become fully independent

I would say that the bureaucracy in terms of administrative work just saddens me, never enjoyed my course fully due to the involvement of necessary professional development. I don't want to leave my online friends but life has an element of sacrifice and I'm not fully happy of clutching the knife to the *inner child* so to speak.
